newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo to issue Comgas bid specs next week.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo to issue Comgas bid specs next week.

text.p: Sao Paulo hopes next week to publish bid specifications to hire consultants to advise on the sale of its gas distribution firm Comgas and concessions to distribute gas, a state official said.

"We would publish the specifications today, but some small items were not in line with privatization rules. I hope we can publish the documents next week," said Sao Paulo state Energy Secretary David Zylbersztajn.
The state plans to hire two consultants, Zylbersztajn said. One will do a financial evaluation of Comgas and set a minimum price for the firm.
The second consultant will make a financial and economic analysis of the firm, design a privization model for Comgas and define concession areas to be privatized, he said.
Comgas is responsible for 30 percent of Brazil's natural gas sales and is expected to privatized in October.
The company is expected to become a leading source of energy in the state in the medium-term, with most of the gas to be used to fuel thermoeletric plants.
Currently, Comgas distributes 3 million cubic metres of gas daily. But it has agreed with Petrobras to increase its daily purchases by 1.5 million cubic metres of gas by 1998.
When the Brazil-Bolivia gas pipeline is completed by 2000, Comgas will purchase another 8 million cubic meters daily.
